author: reek
body: TrackerApp's issue list is a DataTable, and TrackerApp is one of the two GuiOS apps named on the bar. CallPage, WorkflowHtml, RiverPage and Notebook build tables too. None of them had a test.

author: reek
body: The chapter is called a sortable table, so the sort is asked for even though nothing outside this chapter calls it: an unused function that is wrong is a trap laid for the first caller, and the sort rests on comparing two Texts with the ordering operators, which is a primitive worth adjudicating on its own before believing anything built on it.

author: reek
body: The rows are seeded out of order and their first cells are single letters, so a lexicographic sort has exactly one right answer and an insertion-order pass-through is visibly different from it. The third column is built with table-column-fixed, which nothing in the tree calls either, so that the non-sortable path has a row that must NOT move under a sort request.

author: reek
body: Selection is asked on two rows and not one. The table stripes alternate rows by setting a widget state, and a selected row carries a state too, so a row's parity is exactly the axis on which the two can collide. Ask only about row zero and the question is never put.

author: reek
body: A built table is a header, then one panel per visible row, then a footer.

target: section:The comparison the sort rests on
author: reek
body: Before asking whether the sort orders rows, ask what the primitive it sorts with orders by. A sort checked only against its own comparison is checked against nothing.

author: reek
body: Seeded c a e b d. Ascending is a b c d e and descending is e d c b a; either is plainly different from the seeded order, so a sort that did nothing cannot pass as either.

author: reek
body: The sort copies the rows before reordering them, so a caller still holding the table it handed in finds it in the order it built.

author: reek
body: The third column declares itself unsortable, so a sort request on it must leave the order exactly as seeded.

author: reek
body: Row zero is an even stripe and row one is an odd stripe. A selected row must read as selected whichever it lands on.

author: reek
body: Enter selects the row navigation has reached, and does nothing on a table nobody has moved in yet. Both halves are asked: a handler that always selected row zero would pass the first and fail the second.
